_meta.source: 4-agent semantics extraction for remaining rolling/daily factors
_meta.caveat: EMPIRICALLY REFUTED for Beta: min_periods gates on RAW post-join row index, not valid count (proven: emission at 20th row with 13 valid pairs). Treat all min_periods claims as hypotheses to verify by diff.

specs.data_prep: Inputs: monthlyCRSP.parquet [permno, time_avail_m, ret] (L39-41); monthlyFF.parquet [time_avail_m, rf] (L46-48); monthlyMarket.parquet [time_avail_m, ewretd] (L53-55). Joins (L60-64): crsp INNER join ff on time_avail_m, then INNER join market on time_avail_m, sort [permno, time_avail_m]. Inner joins mean a permno-month row exists only if that month is present in BOTH monthlyFF and monthlyMarket — months outside FF coverage (monthly FF starts 1926-07) are removed entirely and never occupy a window position. Excess returns (L73-78): retrf = ret - rf; ewmktrf = ewretd - rf. NOTE: market factor is the EQUAL-weighted CRSP return ewretd minus rf, not vwretd and not FF mktrf. No dedup anywhere — duplicate permno-months (if any existed) would enter windows twice. time_temp = 1..n per permno (L81) is purely positional and redundant with the existing sort (L90 re-sorts by [permno, time_temp], identical order).
specs.window_mechanics: polars-ols least_squares.rolling_ols per permno (L93-104): window_size=60, min_periods=20, null_policy='drop'. VERDICT: POSITIONAL over VALID rows, calendar-agnostic. null_policy='drop' filters out any row where retrf or ewmktrf is null BEFORE rolling; the 60-row window then slides over the surviving (valid) rows only, so a window can span far more than 60 calendar months across listing gaps or missing-ret stretches; dropped rows get null output when results are scattered back to original positions. min_periods=20 counts VALID observations (rows in the filtered stream), not raw rows: output is null for the first 19 valid rows of a permno; valid rows 20-59 use an expanding window (all valid rows so far); from valid row 60 onward a trailing 60-valid-row window. Kernel equivalent: per permno, build the compacted array of (retrf, ewmktrf) pairs where both are finite/non-null, index it k=0..K-1; at compacted index k with k+1>=20, regress over compacted rows [max(0,k-59) .. k]; stamp result at the original row of compacted index k.
specs.computation: OLS with intercept of retrf on ewmktrf; keep slope only. For window rows (x_i=ewmktrf_i, y_i=retrf_i), n=window count: Beta = [n*Σx_iy_i − Σx_i*Σy_i] / [n*Σx_i² − (Σx_i)²]  (equivalently Cov/Var with either dof — ratio is dof-invariant). Intercept b_const is computed (L107) but discarded. 2 parameters, min 20 obs, so no dof shortage. polars-ols solves via normal equations with recursive window updates — one-pass X'X updates can accumulate dust, but for a slope estimate this only bites when Var(x) in the window is ~0 (all ewmktrf equal): exact singularity → null coefficient (row dropped downstream, per established polars-ols behavior); near-singularity/dust → enormous finite Beta that SURVIVES all filters. Kernel should use the same closed-form two-pass or compensated sums; no dof scaling is involved in the output.
specs.output_stamping: The coefficient from the window ENDING at row t is stamped at that row's time_avail_m (signal at month t uses excess returns through month t inclusive; no lag, no skip). Data is already monthly — no monthly collapse. Save path: filter b_ewmktrf.is_not_null() (L113), rename to Beta, to_pandas (L121), save_predictor (L131) → utils/save_standardized.py: pl.from_pandas (nan_to_null=True by default, so NaN→null here), filter is_not_null (L52), yyyymm = year(time_avail_m)*100 + month (L57-64), write CSV [permno, yyyymm, Beta].
specs.edge_semantics: Nulls: null ret/rf/ewretd → row excluded from the regression stream (null_policy='drop') and that row itself gets null Beta → dropped by L113 filter. Singular X'X (zero-variance ewmktrf window) → polars-ols returns null → dropped. NaN outputs (if any escape as NaN rather than null) pass the polars is_not_null at L113 BUT are converted NaN→null by pl.from_pandas inside save_predictor and dropped there — net effect: both null and NaN never reach the CSV. ±inf: inf inputs are 'valid' to the drop policy and propagate into sums → NaN/inf Beta; inf Beta (e.g. from variance dust) is neither null nor NaN and WOULD be written to CSV. No winsorization, no min-price/exchange filters, no dedup.

specs.data_prep: Inputs: monthlyCRSP.parquet [permno, time_avail_m, ret] (L38-40); monthlyFF.parquet [time_avail_m, rf, mktrf, hml, smb] (L45-47); monthlyLiquidity.parquet [time_avail_m, ps_innov] (L52-54). Joins (L59-63): crsp INNER join ff on time_avail_m, then LEFT join liquidity on time_avail_m (comment L61: 'Keep missing liquidity obs' — rows for months absent from the liquidity file survive with ps_innov=null), sort [permno, time_avail_m]. Excess return (L72): retrf = ret - rf. Only the stock return gets the rf subtraction; ps_innov, mktrf, hml, smb enter as-is. LIQUIDITY-SERIES ENTRY POINT (for the planned point-in-time swap): ps_innov is a single market-wide monthly scalar joined by time_avail_m only; the regression mechanics are fully separable from its source — the kernel should take an aligned monthly vector ps_innov[t] as an input series. CRITICAL COUPLING to record: because the join is LEFT but null_policy='drop', the NULL PATTERN of the liquidity series determines which rows enter windows — months before the PS innovation series begins (or any gap in it) are excluded from the valid-row stream and do not advance window positions. A rebuilt PIT series with different coverage will shift every window's composition, not just the regressor values.
specs.window_mechanics: polars-ols least_squares.rolling_ols per permno (L86-100): target retrf on 4 regressors (ps_innov, mktrf, hml, smb) + intercept, window_size=60, min_periods=36, null_policy='drop'. VERDICT: POSITIONAL over VALID rows, calendar-agnostic — a row is valid only if ALL of retrf, ps_innov, mktrf, hml, smb are non-null (so pre-liquidity-coverage months never count, even though the left join kept them). Window = trailing 60 valid rows ending at the current valid row; min_periods=36 counts valid rows: null output for the first 35 valid rows, expanding window for valid rows 36-59, trailing 60 thereafter. Dropped (null-bearing) rows get null output at their original positions. time_temp (L75, 1-indexed) again redundant with the time sort (L84).
specs.computation: OLS with intercept: retrf = const + b_ps*ps_innov + b_mkt*mktrf + b_hml*hml + b_smb*smb; solve the 5x5 normal equations (X'X)b = X'y over the window and keep ONLY b_ps_innov as BetaLiquidityPS (L104, L113-116); b_const/b_mktrf/b_hml/b_smb extracted then discarded. 5 parameters vs min 36 obs. Kernel: accumulate X'X (5x5 symmetric incl. intercept column of ones) and X'y over window rows, solve by Cholesky/LU; declare singular → null (matching polars-ols null-on-singular → row dropped). One-pass accumulation caveat: with 4 correlated regressors near-collinearity (e.g. ps_innov nearly spanned by mktrf/hml/smb in a short window) produces ill-conditioned solves — the reference's recursive updates yield either null (exact singular, dropped) or huge finite coefficients (kept); use the same solve-or-null rule, no ridge, no pinv.
specs.output_stamping: Coefficient from the window ending at row t stamped at that row's time_avail_m (through month t inclusive, no lag). No monthly collapse (already monthly). Filters: L113 b_ps_innov.is_not_null(), then a second redundant is_not_null on the renamed column (L116). to_pandas (L122) → save_predictor (L132): pl.from_pandas NaN→null, drop nulls, yyyymm = year*100+month, CSV [permno, yyyymm, BetaLiquidityPS].
specs.edge_semantics: Any null among {ret, rf, ps_innov, mktrf, hml, smb} removes the row from the valid stream AND nulls its own output → dropped at L113/L116. Singular/rank-deficient windows → null → dropped. NaN coefficients would survive L113/L116 (polars is_not_null keeps NaN) but die in save_predictor's pl.from_pandas(nan_to_null=True) → net: no null/NaN in CSV. ±inf coefficients (near-singular dust) are kept and written. No dedup; FF and liquidity are m:1 monthly joins so cannot fan out rows. Coverage note (f): effective sample start per permno = first month with all five series present — i.e. max(CRSP start, FF monthly start 1926-07, PS innovation series start), then +35 more valid months before first output.

specs.data_prep: Inputs: monthlyCRSP.parquet [permno, time_avail_m, ret] (L41-43); monthlyFF.parquet [time_avail_m, rf, mktrf, hml, smb] (L48-50). Join (L55): crsp INNER join ff on time_avail_m (Stata merge keep(match) equivalent) — CRSP months outside FF monthly coverage (starts 1926-07) vanish. Excess return (L63): retrf = ret - rf. Sort [permno, time_avail_m] (L67); time_temp = 0..n-1 per permno (L71), positional, redundant with the sort (L83). Script emits TWO signals: ResidualMomentum (11-window, saved as predictor via save_predictor L183) and ResidualMomentum6m (6-window, saved as placebo via save_placebo L178). No dedup.
specs.window_mechanics: TWO DISTINCT window regimes — this is the key fidelity trap. STAGE 1 (residuals, L85-99): polars-ols rolling_ols per permno, retrf on (mktrf, hml, smb) + intercept, window_size=36, min_periods=36, mode='residuals', null_policy='drop' → POSITIONAL over VALID rows (rows with retrf/mktrf/hml/smb all non-null): output at valid row k (k 0-indexed) exists only when k>=35 and equals the residual of row k from the regression fit on the trailing 36 valid rows ending at k (exactly 36, never expanding, since min_periods=window_size); null-input rows get null residual at their original position. STAGE 2 (momentum, L107-139): temp = residual shift(1) over permno (L110-113) — a POSITIONAL lag over ALL original rows (not valid rows): temp at row t = residual of the previous PHYSICAL row, whatever month that was. Then pl rolling_mean/rolling_std with window_size=6, min_samples=6 and window_size=11, min_samples=11 (ddof=1) over permno (L118-139) — these are plain polars rolling windows over PHYSICAL rows where min_samples counts NON-NULL values inside the window: since window_size==min_samples, ALL 6 (resp. 11) consecutive physical rows must have non-null temp or the output is null. So stage 1 tolerates gaps (compacts over them); stage 2 does NOT — any null residual (from a dropped input row or insufficient history) inside the trailing 6/11 physical rows nulls the signal. Earliest possible signal: valid row 36 gives first residual; +1 shift; +11 window → physical row >= 47 assuming no gaps.
specs.computation: Stage 1 per window: solve 4-parameter OLS (const, mktrf, hml, smb) over 36 obs, residual_t = retrf_t − [b0 + b1*mktrf_t + b2*hml_t + b3*smb_t] where t is the LAST row of the window — each month's residual comes from a DIFFERENT regression (window ending at that month), matching Stata asreg rolling residuals; residuals for interior window rows are never used. Stage 2: mean_w = arithmetic mean of temp over trailing w physical rows; sd_w = sample std, ddof=1 (explicit at L126/L136): sd = sqrt( Σ(temp_i − mean)² / (w−1) ). Signals (L142-148): ResidualMomentum6m = mean6/sd6, ResidualMomentum = mean11/sd11. In month terms for row t: ResidualMomentum uses residuals of physical rows t-11..t-1 (skips month t itself via the shift). Kernel: two-pass (mean then squared deviations) for sd to avoid one-pass negative-variance dust — but note the REFERENCE uses polars' rolling one-pass kernels, so exact-zero-sd windows may show dust there (see edges).
specs.output_stamping: Signal stamped at time_avail_m of row t (the row whose trailing lagged-residual window it is); information content ends at month t-1 (residual lag built in). No monthly collapse. Save: select + to_pandas (L173-175); save_placebo(ResidualMomentum6m) L178, save_predictor(ResidualMomentum) L183 — both do pl.from_pandas (NaN→null via default nan_to_null=True), filter is_not_null, yyyymm = year*100+month, CSV. Note the full df (all rows incl. nulls) goes to the save functions; the null-drop happens entirely inside save_*.
specs.edge_semantics: Null handling: null retrf/factor → row dropped from stage-1 stream + null residual at that row → poisons every 6/11-physical-row window containing it → null signal → dropped at save. Singular stage-1 window (rank-deficient factors, essentially impossible for FF3 over 36 months) → null residual, same poisoning. Division edges (d): if all 11 temps are equal, true sd=0 → mean/0 = ±inf (kept: inf is neither null nor NaN, written to CSV) and 0/0 = NaN (dropped at save via from_pandas NaN→null); BUT polars' one-pass rolling_std can return ~1e-17 dust instead of exact 0, turning would-be inf/NaN into a huge finite value that is kept — a numba kernel with exact two-pass arithmetic will hit exact 0 where the reference hits dust; this is the main potential mismatch source. skew() not used here; std is explicitly ddof=1 (b). inf residual inputs (from inf ret) propagate through mean/sd untouched. Physical-row lag caveat: shift(1) and the 6/11 windows never look at calendar months — a permno with a delisting gap gets residuals from non-adjacent months averaged together as if consecutive, provided none are null.

specs.data_prep: monthlyCRSP.parquet [permno, time_avail_m, ret] INNER-joined to monthlyFF.parquet [time_avail_m, mktrf, rf] on time_avail_m (L46-48), then filter mktrf NOT NULL AND rf NOT NULL (L48). Months absent from FF (monthly FF starts 1926-07) drop the stock rows entirely — they never enter any window as rows. Excess returns (L53-55): ret := ret - rf (simple excess; ret may be NULL and stays NULL), mkt := mktrf (already excess). No shrcd/exchange filter, no date filter. time_avail_m_int = (year-1960)*12 + (month-1) (L63-70).
specs.window_mechanics: CALENDAR window built via a 60-batch modulo trick, not a positional roll. Sort permno asc / time desc (L60); m60 = time_int % 60 (L70). For each batch m in 0..59: rows with m60==m get stamp = their own time_int, others NULL (L87-94); forward_fill over permno in DESCENDING time order (L97-104) so every row is assigned to the NEXT (future) data-bearing month of the permno with month-index ≡ m (mod 60); unstamped rows (newer than the permno's latest such month in this batch) are dropped (L107). Net effect across all 60 batches: EVERY permno-month with a post-join row becomes an anchor t exactly once, and its group contains the permno's rows with calendar month index in (t_prev, t], where t_prev is the permno's most recent DATA-BEARING month ≡ t (mod 60). When the permno has an observation exactly at t-60 this is precisely the trailing 60 calendar months [t-59, t]; if the permno lacks a row at t-60 (or at its first cycle month after listing), OLDER rows LEAK IN — the window extends back to the previous existing anchor, potentially unbounded. Verdict: calendar 60-month trailing window over the permno's available monthly rows, with the gap-leak quirk above. Min-obs (L140-149, L161): nobs = count() of non-null ret_demeaned in the group, i.e. counts VALID ret values (NULL-ret rows in the window do NOT count); require nobs >= 12. No cross-sectional filter.
specs.computation: Two-pass demeaned sample moments per (permno, anchor) group, all POPULATION means (polars .mean() = sum/count-of-non-null; no ddof anywhere, .std()/.skew() never used). Pass 1 (L115-128): E_ret = mean of non-null ret over group; E_mkt = mean of mkt over ALL rows of group (mkt never null post-filter). ret_demeaned = ret - E_ret (NULL where ret NULL); mkt_demeaned = mkt - E_mkt. Pass 2 (L131-158): E_ret_mkt2 = mean(ret_demeaned * mkt_demeaned^2) over rows with valid ret only (nulls skipped); E_ret2 = mean(ret_demeaned^2) over valid-ret rows; E_mkt2 = mean(mkt_demeaned^2) over ALL rows in the group INCLUDING null-ret rows. Coskewness = E_ret_mkt2 / ( sqrt(E_ret2) * E_mkt2 ) (L152-158) — Harvey-Siddique: note denominator uses E_mkt2, NOT its sqrt. FIDELITY ASYMMETRY: market moments (E_mkt, E_mkt2) average over all window rows; stock moments average over valid-ret rows only — a kernel that pre-filters null-ret rows before computing market moments deviates.
specs.output_stamping: Group value lands at the anchor month t = the MOST RECENT month of the window (the window includes month t itself; no lag). yyyymm = (1960 + t//12)*100 + (t%12 + 1) (L183-192). One row per permno-month present post-join. Saved via direct write_csv (L203) — NOT save_predictor: NO null/NaN drop at save time; NaN values (see edges) are written to Coskewness.csv.
specs.edge_semantics: NULL ret rows survive the join and sit inside windows (contribute to market moments and row membership, not to stock moments or nobs). 0/0: if the stock's valid rets are all equal in the window, E_ret2 = 0 and E_ret_mkt2 = exactly 0 (two-pass demeaning gives exact zeros, no one-pass dust) -> 0.0/0.0 = NaN in polars float division; NaN is NOT null, passes the nobs filter, and is written to CSV. Nonzero/0 -> ±inf kept (practically impossible: E_mkt2=0 requires constant market). No log transforms, so no inf from ret=-1. Post nobs>=12 filter the moments themselves are never null, so no nulls reach the CSV — only possible NaN/inf. No dedup needed: each anchor month falls in exactly one of the 60 batches, so concat (L178) produces unique (permno, yyyymm). Anchor row itself may have NULL ret; the group still exists and is stamped at t.

specs.data_prep: dailyCRSP.parquet [permno, time_d, ret], HARD FILTER time_d >= 1962-07-02 (L39). INNER join dailyFF [time_d, mktrf, rf] on time_d, filter mktrf/rf NOT NULL (L51-53) — only days present in daily FF survive (FF daily starts 1926-07, so the 1962 filter binds). Total market return mkt_raw = mktrf + rf (L58). LOG excess returns (L63-68): mkt := ln(1+mktrf+rf) - ln(1+rf); ret := ln(1+ret) - ln(1+rf). NULL ret stays NULL. Sort permno asc / time_d desc (L73).
specs.window_mechanics: CALENDAR trailing 12-month window via 12-batch modulo trick. For batch m in 1..12: every daily row whose calendar month == m gets stamp = (year-1960)*12+(month-1) (all days of that month share one stamp, L88-98); forward_fill over permno in DESCENDING date order (L101-107); null-stamped rows (newer than the permno's latest month-m occurrence) dropped (L111). Group for anchor month t (a permno-month with >=1 daily row): all the permno's daily rows dated after the end of the permno's previous DATA-BEARING calendar-month-m occurrence, through the end of month t — normally exactly the 12 calendar months [t-11, t] inclusive of the anchor month's own days. Gap leak: if the permno has no rows in month m of the prior year, older daily rows leak into this anchor's window (window extends to the previous existing same-calendar-month occurrence). Every permno-month with data becomes an anchor exactly once across the 12 batches. Verdict: calendar 12-month window over available daily rows. MIN-OBS IS RELATIVE AND CROSS-SECTIONAL (L162-168): nobs = count of non-null ret_demeaned (valid ret days) per (permno, t); max_nobs = max of nobs across ALL permnos sharing stamp t (each stamp lives in exactly one batch, so this is a per-output-month cross-sectional max); keep iff max_nobs - nobs <= 5. There is NO absolute minimum. A streaming per-stock kernel needs the cross-sectional max of valid-day counts for the month before filtering — note max_nobs can be inflated by a gap-leak stock with an over-long window.
specs.computation: Identical two-pass demeaned population-moment structure to Coskewness (L119-160), on daily LOG excess returns: E_ret (mean over valid-ret rows), E_mkt (mean over ALL group rows); demean; E_ret_mkt2 = mean(ret_dm * mkt_dm^2) and E_ret2 = mean(ret_dm^2) over valid-ret rows; E_mkt2 = mean(mkt_dm^2) over ALL rows including null-ret rows. CoskewACX = E_ret_mkt2 / ( sqrt(E_ret2) * E_mkt2 ) (L154-160) — denominator uses E_mkt2 (variance), not SD; the ABOUTME comment 'SD[r]*SD[m]^2' describes the population formula this sample version implements since moments are population means. All divisions by count of non-null contributing values. Same market/stock moment asymmetry fidelity trap as Coskewness.
specs.output_stamping: Value for anchor month t stamped at yyyymm = (1960 + t//12)*100 + (t%12 + 1) (L190-199); window INCLUDES month t (no lag). One row per permno-month with >=1 post-join daily row that passes the relative-nobs filter. Direct write_csv (L210) — no null/NaN drop at save.
specs.edge_semantics: LOG TRANSFORM INF: ret == -1 -> ln(0) = -inf (kept by polars); ret < -1 -> ln(negative) = NaN. A -inf in a window makes E_ret = -inf, ret_demeaned = NaN (for that row: -inf-(-inf)) or +inf (other rows), E_ret2/E_ret_mkt2 = NaN -> CoskewACX = NaN, which is NOT null: it passes count() (NaN counts as valid), passes the relative filter, and is WRITTEN to CSV. 0/0 (constant valid rets, e.g. all-zero after log) -> exact 0/0 = NaN kept — two-pass demeaning gives exact zero numerator/denominator, no one-pass dust. If a stamp group has zero valid rets, moments are NULL; it survives the relative filter only when max_nobs <= 5 (tiny early cross-sections) and a NULL would then be written. NULL ret rows: excluded from stock moments and nobs but INCLUDED in E_mkt/E_mkt2 and window membership. No dedup needed (each stamp in exactly one batch). Days absent from dailyFF never enter any window.

specs.data_prep: PART 1 — tail-risk factor (L37-87): dailyCRSP [permno, time_d, ret], NO date filter, NO FF join, RAW returns (no excess construction anywhere in this script). time_avail_m = calendar month of time_d (dt.truncate('1mo'), L43-45). retp5 per month = 5th percentile of ALL daily rets pooled across all stocks that month, polars quantile(0.05, interpolation='lower') (L51-53): sort non-null rets ascending, take element at index floor(0.05*(n-1)) — an actual data point, so >=1 row always ties. Inner-join retp5 back on month (L59); keep rows ret <= retp5 inclusive (L65; NULL ret comparisons are null -> dropped). tailex = ln(ret / retp5) (L69-71). Monthly factor = arithmetic mean of tailex over all tail rows that month (L77-81); written to ../pyData/Intermediate/TailRisk.parquet (L86). PART 2 (L94-104): monthlyCRSP [permno, time_avail_m, ret, shrcd] (raw monthly ret, NOT excess) LEFT-joined to the monthly tailex series on time_avail_m — months before daily-data start or without a tail factor get NULL tailex. SEPARABILITY (for the planned point-in-time series swap, same pattern as BetaLiquidityPS/ps_innov): the regression consumes ONLY a monthly scalar series keyed by time_avail_m entering via this single left join at L101; Part 1 is fully severable — swap the series source and Part 2's mechanics below are unchanged.
specs.window_mechanics: polars_ols rolling_ols per permno (L127-144): y = raw monthly ret, X = [tailex, intercept], window_size=120, min_periods=72, null_policy='drop', mode='coefficients', sorted by (permno, time_avail_m_int) (L125). CRITICAL — null_policy='drop' (NOT 'drop_window'): per polars_ols least_squares.py L47-56, 'drop' removes any row with a null in target or features BEFORE fitting and masks those rows' outputs with null, whereas 'drop_window' would keep a fixed positional window and omit nulls inside it. So the window is the trailing 120 VALID rows (both ret and tailex non-null) of the permno's joined monthly series — POSITIONAL over valid observations, NOT 120 calendar months: calendar gaps in monthlyCRSP rows and null-tailex/null-ret months stretch the calendar span. min_periods=72 counts VALID observations (warm-up: first coefficient appears at the permno's 72nd valid row). Rows that are themselves invalid (null ret or null tailex) get NULL output even if 120 prior valid obs exist. Verdict: positional-over-valid-rows, min-obs counts valid pairs.
specs.computation: Per output row t: OLS of ret on [1, tailex] over the last min(n_valid_so_far, 120) valid (ret, tailex) pairs up to and INCLUDING row t; BetaTailRisk = slope on tailex (struct field 'tailex', L140-147; intercept field 'const' discarded). Numba equivalent: over the window, b_tailex = sum((x-xbar)(y-ybar)) / sum((x-xbar)^2), b_const = ybar - b_tailex*xbar; coefficients only, no dof adjustment anywhere (no stderr computed). alpha unset -> pure OLS, use_woodbury default false for 2 features. Post-regression filters (L150-152): BetaTailRisk IS NOT NULL and shrcd <= 11 (keeps 10/11 common shares; NULL shrcd compares null -> dropped). Note shrcd filter applies at OUTPUT time only — non-common months still supply observations inside windows.
specs.output_stamping: Coefficient at valid row t is stamped at that row's time_avail_m (contemporaneous: window includes month t's ret and tailex; no lag). save_predictor (utils/save_standardized.py L32-83): drops NULL BetaTailRisk (redundant after L151), yyyymm = year*100 + month of time_avail_m, writes [permno, yyyymm, BetaTailRisk] CSV. NaN is NOT null — a NaN beta survives both is_not_null (L151) and save_predictor's filter and is written to CSV.
specs.edge_semantics: NULL vs NaN: null_policy='drop' drops NULLS only — a NaN tailex month (see below) is treated as VALID and poisons every 120-row window containing it (NaN coefficients emitted, saved as NaN). Tail-factor NaN/inf sources (theoretical, require a month whose pooled 5th percentile >= 0): retp5=0 with ret<0 -> ln(neg)=NaN; ret=0 with retp5=0 -> ln(0/0)=NaN; ret=0 only enters the tail when retp5>=0. Normal months (retp5<0, ret<=retp5<0) give finite tailex>=0. Singular window (zero tailex variance across the 120 valid rows): polars_ols solves normal equations -> NaN (not null) coefficients expected -> NaN row saved; genuinely NULL outputs occur only for warm-up (<72 valid), masked invalid rows, and are dropped at L151/save. Monthly quantile: polars 'lower' skips nulls, index floor(0.05*(n-1)) on ascending sort. No dedup concerns (one row per permno-month in monthlyCRSP). Left join means pre-1926 (or pre-daily-coverage) months exist as rows with null tailex — they are dropped from fitting, NOT counted toward the 120/72, and produce no output.

specs.data_prep: NOTE: DAILY data, not weekly. (L52-57) dailyFF.parquet select [time_d, mktrf, rf], sort time_d, then mktLag{n} = mktrf.shift(n) for n=1..4 computed on the FULL FF trading calendar BEFORE any join — so lags are market-calendar lags (previous FF trading days), independent of the stock's missing days; first 4 FF rows (1926-07) have null lags. (L64-69) dailyCRSP [permno,time_d,ret] INNER join FF on time_d — stock days without FF drop (FF daily starts 1926-07); CRSP null-ret rows survive the join. (L72) ret := ret - rf (excess simple return, overwrites ret); mktrf used as-is (already excess). (L97-106) group key: time_m = time_d truncated to month; time_avail_m = June 1 of year(time_m + 6mo) → annual buckets spanning July 1 (y-1) through June 30 (y), keyed June y. (L111) sort [time_avail_m, permno, time_d].
specs.window_mechanics: CALENDAR-PERIOD window, not rolling and not positional: one regression per (permno, July(y-1)–June(y) bucket) over whatever joined daily rows fall in that bucket — gaps irrelevant. Min-obs (L116-138), ALL required per group: pl.len() >= 26 (raw row count INCLUDING null-ret rows); ret.count() >= 26 AND mktrf.count() >= 26 (non-null counts); ret.var() > 0 and not null, mktrf.var() > 0 and not null (polars .var() ddof=1, computed over non-null values only). No check on lag nulls — inside the regression null_policy='drop' additionally drops any row where ret, mktrf, or any mktLag1..4 is null, so effective n can be < 26 only at the 1926-07 sample start. Additional survival filter (L248-257): the group's LAST time_d (data sorted by time_d within group, .last()) must have month == 6, i.e. the stock must trade at least one June day in the bucket; stocks delisting before June drop the whole year. VERDICT: calendar-bucket regression; min-obs counts both raw rows and non-null values, both thresholds = 26.
specs.computation: Unrestricted OLS per group (L180-203): ret_excess ~ intercept + b0*mktrf + b1*mktLag1 + b2*mktLag2 + b3*mktLag3 + b4*mktLag4, via polars_ols least_squares.ols(add_intercept=True, null_policy='drop', solve_method='svd'), run twice (mode='coefficients' for betas, mode='statistics' for r2/t_values). weightscale = 1 (L47). PriceDelaySlope = (1*b1 + 2*b2 + 3*b3 + 4*b4) / (b0 + b1 + b2 + b3 + b4) (L272-281, sum_horizontal). Residual dof for the statistics struct = n_valid - 6 (5 slopes + intercept). SVD solve: singular design does NOT error — returns min-norm coefficients, so no group is dropped for collinearity among lags (zero-variance mktrf groups were pre-filtered).
specs.output_stamping: Regression value for bucket July(y-1)–June(y) is stamped time_avail_m = June-1(y) then offset +1mo (L301-303) → July y (yyyymm = y*100+7). The '📊 Applying winsorization' print is a lie — NO winsorization is applied. Forward-fill to monthly (L308-383): per permno, monthly grid from min July stamp to max July stamp, left-join computed values, forward_fill().over(permno) each of the 3 columns — each annual value propagates July→following June (11 fills); a missing year forward-fills straight across the gap (unbounded within the grid); the LAST annual value gets ZERO forward-fill months because the grid ends at the last July stamp. save_predictor drops null rows only; yyyymm = year*100 + month.
specs.edge_semantics: Group survival requires only _R2 (unrestricted r2) not null + June endpoint (L255-257) — R2Restricted null does not drop the group for Slope/Tstat. Denominator b0+sum(b_lags) == 0 → ±inf (or NaN if numerator also 0); inf/NaN are NOT nulled anywhere and pass save_predictor's is_not_null filter → written to CSV. forward_fill fills nulls only, so a NaN annual value forward-fills as NaN. No dedup of (permno,time_d) anywhere — duplicates would double-count in regressions. null_policy='drop' asymmetry: restricted regression drops rows on {ret,mktrf} nulls, unrestricted on {ret,mktrf,lags} nulls, so the two regressions can run on different row sets (matters only at 1926-07).

specs.data_prep: Identical to PriceDelaySlope (same script, same joined frame, same groups): FF lags built on market calendar pre-join (L52-57); inner join on time_d (L69); ret := ret - rf (L72); annual July–June buckets keyed June y (L97-106).
specs.window_mechanics: Identical to PriceDelaySlope: calendar July–June bucket, min 26 raw rows AND min 26 non-null ret AND min 26 non-null mktrf, var(ret)>0, var(mktrf)>0 (ddof=1 over non-null), last trading day in bucket must be in June, null_policy='drop' inside each regression.
specs.computation: Two regressions per group: restricted OLS ret_excess ~ intercept + mktrf (L166-176, mode='statistics') giving R2Restricted = struct field 'r2'; unrestricted OLS ret_excess ~ intercept + mktrf + mktLag1..4 giving _R2 (L213-218). PriceDelayRsq = 1 - R2Restricted / _R2 (L264-266). r2 = 1 - SSE/SST with intercept (standard centered R²), restricted dof n-2, unrestricted dof n-6.
specs.output_stamping: Identical to PriceDelaySlope: stamped July y (June key + 1mo, L301-303), forward-filled monthly per permno July→June, last annual value not forward-filled, save_predictor drops nulls, yyyymm = year*100+month.
specs.edge_semantics: Because null_policy='drop' can give the restricted regression MORE rows than the unrestricted one (lag nulls), model nesting is not guaranteed → R2Restricted > _R2 possible → negative PriceDelayRsq (kept). One-pass/SVD r2 arithmetic: near-perfect fits can yield _R2 with negative-SSE dust ≈ 1 + eps or R2Restricted marginally above _R2 → tiny negative values (kept). _R2 == 0 exactly → R2Restricted/0 = inf (or NaN if 0/0) → 1-inf = -inf, NOT nulled, survives save_predictor (only nulls dropped). _R2 null → group dropped for ALL three predictors (L256). R2Restricted null with _R2 valid → PriceDelayRsq null → that row dropped at save time for Rsq only, Slope/Tstat still saved.

specs.data_prep: Identical to PriceDelaySlope (same script, same frame, same groups).
specs.window_mechanics: Identical to PriceDelaySlope: calendar July–June bucket, min 26 raw rows / 26 non-null ret / 26 non-null mktrf, positive variances, June-endpoint requirement, null_policy='drop'.
specs.computation: From the unrestricted regression statistics struct (mode='statistics', L192-201): t_values is a list ordered [mktrf, mktLag1, mktLag2, mktLag3, mktLag4, const] (L229-241); t_j = b_j / se_j with se from sigma^2 * diag((X'X)^-1), sigma^2 = SSE/(n_valid - 6). PriceDelayTstat = (1*t_lag1 + 2*t_lag2 + 3*t_lag3 + 4*t_lag4) / (t_mktrf + t_lag1 + t_lag2 + t_lag3 + t_lag4) (L287-296, weightscale=1). Unlike Hou-Moskowitz, NO precision-weight denominators beyond the raw t's — the formula is exactly the weighted-t ratio above.
specs.output_stamping: Identical to PriceDelaySlope: July-y stamp, monthly forward-fill within [first July, last July] grid per permno, save_predictor drops nulls only.
specs.edge_semantics: Perfect-fit groups (SSE ≈ 0) give se → 0 → t = ±inf or NaN (0/0); with SVD pseudo-inverse on singular X'X, se can be 0 or garbage → inf/NaN t's. inf t's propagate through the ratio: inf/inf = NaN (kept, saved as NaN), finite/inf = 0. Denominator t_mktrf + sum(t_lags) == 0 → ±inf (kept). None of inf/NaN are nulled; only genuinely-null t_values (regression returned null struct) make the value null and hence dropped by save_predictor.

specs.data_prep: (L33-42) dailyCRSP [permno,time_d,ret] INNER join dailyFF [time_d,rf,mktrf] on time_d — stock days without FF drop. (L47-53) CRITICAL with_columns semantics: all three expressions evaluate against the INPUT frame, so LogRet = log1p(RAW ret) — NOT excess — while 'ret' is simultaneously overwritten to ret-rf (and then never used again); LogMkt = log1p(mktrf) where mktrf IS excess-of-rf. Asymmetry is real script behavior: stock leg raw log return, market leg excess log return. (L56) sort [permno, time_d]. No dedup anywhere.
specs.window_mechanics: All windows are POSITIONAL over the permno's post-join rows (row-count windows, not calendar days; gaps compress). (L62-73) sd252_LogRet and sd252_LogMkt: rolling_std(window_size=252, min_samples=120).over('permno'), ddof=1; min_samples counts NON-NULL values inside the 252-row window (null-ret rows occupy positions but don't count). sd252_LogMkt is the MARKET vol computed over the STOCK's own rows — a stock with missing days gets a different market vol than the full calendar would give. (L79-91) 3-day overlapping returns: tempRi = LogRet + LogRet.shift(1) + LogRet.shift(2) over permno (positional shifts; null if any of the 3 is null; first 2 rows per permno null); tempRm identically from LogMkt, also shifted within the permno's rows. (L97-121) rolling corr inputs: window_size=1260 rows, min_samples=500 non-null, per permno. VERDICT: positional row windows throughout; min-obs counts non-null values, not rows.
specs.computation: (L102-130) One-pass population covariance: cov_temp = rolling_mean(tempRi*tempRm) - rolling_mean(tempRi)*rolling_mean(tempRm) (each 1260/500); std_tempRi, std_tempRm = rolling_std(1260, 500) ddof=1 (SAMPLE). corr_hat = cov_temp/(std_tempRi*std_tempRm) → MIXED ddof: population cov over sample stds ⇒ corr_hat = true_corr * (n-1)/n when null patterns align. _R2 = corr_hat^2 (L126-129). (L135-141) BetaFP = sqrt(abs(_R2)) * (sd252_LogRet / sd252_LogMkt) = |corr_hat| * vol_ratio — the SIGN of the correlation is destroyed; BetaFP >= 0 always. Note vol ratio uses 1-day log-return stds (252/120) while corr uses 3-day overlapping returns (1260/500).
specs.output_stamping: (L147-158) time_avail_m = time_d truncated to month; filter BetaFP.is_finite() FIRST (drops null, NaN, ±inf — null is_finite→null→filtered); sort [permno, time_avail_m, time_d]; group_by(permno, time_avail_m).agg(last()) → the LAST finite BetaFP within the month (latest qualifying trading day, which need not be the month's last trading day if that day's value was non-finite). NO month lag: month-m value stamped yyyymm of month m itself. save_predictor drops nulls (none remain post-filter).
specs.edge_semantics: rolling_mean/rolling_std skip nulls (aggregate over non-null in window) once min_samples non-null met — and the three rolling_means in the cov formula can aggregate over DIFFERENT row sets when tempRi is null but tempRm isn't (stock null-ret days mid-sample): E[xy] and E[x] exclude those rows, E[y] includes them ⇒ internally inconsistent cov. One-pass cov ⇒ catastrophic cancellation possible; |corr_hat| can exceed 1 slightly (dust), _R2 > 1 kept — abs() before sqrt guards only sign, not magnitude. std_tempRi or std_tempRm == 0 ⇒ corr = ±inf or NaN ⇒ BetaFP inf/NaN ⇒ removed by the is_finite monthly filter (this is the ONLY inf/NaN gate in the script). sd252_LogMkt == 0 ⇒ inf, same gate. ret <= -1 ⇒ log1p → -inf or NaN, propagates into windows until aged out, downstream infs caught by the same gate. min_samples not met ⇒ null ⇒ filtered at monthly step.

specs.data_prep: STAGE 1 (daily, L1361-1434): dailyCRSP.parquet cols [permno, time_d, prc, cfacpr]. P = abs(prc)/cfacpr (L1374; null prc or null cfacpr -> null P; cfacpr==0 -> +inf, polars float division). Sort [permno, time_d] (L1378); time_temp = 0..n-1 row counter per permno (L1379-1381); time_avail_m = month-truncated time_d (L1384-1386). For each L in {3,5,10,20,50,100,200,400,600,800,1000}: A_L = asrol rolling mean of P (see window_mechanics). Monthly collapse: sort [permno,time_avail_m,time_d], group_by(permno,time_avail_m).last() -> last TRADING row present per stock-month (L1421-1422). Normalize: A_L := A_L / P using that last-day P (L1427-1430). temp_ma = [permno, time_avail_m, A_3..A_1000]. STAGE 2 (monthly, L1444-1499): SignalMasterTable.parquet cols [permno, time_avail_m, ret, prc, exchcd, shrcd, mve_c]. Per month, qu10 = stata_quantile(mve_c of exchcd==1 rows, 0.10) (L1452-1460; NaNs dropped, stable sort; P=0.10*n; if P within 1e-12 of integer k, value = (arr[k-1]+arr[k])/2, else arr[floor(P)] i.e. the (floor(P)+1)-th order stat); left-join qu10 on month. Filters (L1469-1474): exchcd in {1,2,3} AND shrcd in {10,11} AND stata_ineq abs(prc)>=5 AND stata_ineq mve_c>=qu10. CRITICAL stata_ineq_pl semantics (stata_replication.py L415-475): nulls fill to +inf on BOTH sides for >=, so null prc PASSES the >=5 filter and null mve_c PASSES the size filter; null qu10 passes only rows with null mve_c. Then INNER join temp_ma on [permno, time_avail_m] (L1479) — stock-months without daily data drop. fRet (L1488-1499): templead = reg_input itself with time_avail_m shifted -1mo, ret renamed fRet; LEFT join back on [permno, time_avail_m]. So fRet(t) = ret(t+1), but ONLY if the stock also survives the filters AND the MA inner-join at t+1; otherwise fRet null (excluded from that month's regression, but the row still gets a TrendFactor).
specs.window_mechanics: DAILY MA (L1397-1410 -> utils/asrol.py L20-99): asrol called with time_col='time_temp', freq='1d', min_samples=1. time_temp (0..n-1 int per permno) is cast to pl.Date (days since epoch); fill_date_gaps_pl builds per-permno date_ranges between min and max — since time_temp is consecutive, NO rows are added, so the window is purely POSITIONAL over the stock's trading rows as present in dailyCRSP (calendar gaps ignored). A_L(d) = polars rolling_mean(window_size=L, min_samples=1) over P per permno: mean of NON-NULL P among the last min(L, rows-so-far) rows including current; min_samples counts NON-NULL values, so A_L is null only when all values in the window are null. Partial windows at series start are allowed (Stata asrol default). BETA SMOOTHING (L1532-1540): betas_by_month has one row per month PRESENT in reg_input, sorted ascending (pandas groupby sorts keys). EBeta_L = _b_A_L.shift(1).rolling_mean(window_size=12, min_samples=1) — POSITIONAL over rows/months present, not calendar-aware (no gap fill); equals mean of non-null betas over months t-12..t-1 when months are contiguous; >=1 non-null beta in the window required, else null (first month always null). NaN monthly betas (failed regressions) are skipped by the mean. CROSS-SECTIONAL REGRESSION: window=None, no min_obs — any month with >=1 valid row runs; verdict: both rolling constructs are positional-over-valid/present rows, not calendar.
specs.computation: Per month t, cross-sectional OLS (asreg_collinear window=None -> _asreg_cross_sectional L497-695 -> regress L216-298): fRet_i = cons + sum_L b_L * A_L_i + e_i, 11 regressors + intercept. Estimation sample: listwise np.isfinite on fRet AND all 11 A_L (L96-106) — both NaN AND +/-inf rows excluded. Collinearity (drop_collinear L46-213): constant columns (max==min) dropped first; then QR with column pivoting on L2-column-normalized remaining X, tol = eps*max(n,p)*max|diag(R)|; rank-deficient columns dropped. DROPPED columns get coefficient 0.0, NOT NaN (L277, L593) — with n < 12 valid rows extra columns are dropped this way and their zero betas later drag EBeta toward 0. Kept columns fit via statsmodels sm.OLS with sm.add_constant (pinv-based, two-pass — trap (d) does not bite here; no negative-SSE dust issue since only betas are consumed downstream, _R2/_sigma unused). No SEs computed (compute_se=False). If a month's group throws (e.g. zero valid rows -> drop_collinear ValueError), the try/except at L624-628 sets ALL result cols NaN for that month. EBeta_L(t) = 12-month trailing mean of b_L (see window_mechanics). SIGNAL (L1552-1583): TrendFactor_i(t) = sum over the 11 L of EBeta_L(t) * A_L_i(t), computed via long unpivot + left join on (time_avail_m, lag) + polars sum. Guard: N_MA_used = count of non-null EBeta_MA terms must == 11 (polars sum of nulls is 0, hence the guard). NOTE: polars counts NaN as NOT-null, so a NaN term (e.g. 0/0 in A_L normalization) passes the ==11 gate and yields NaN TrendFactor.
specs.output_stamping: TrendFactor_i(t) uses month-t MAs and betas estimated through month t-1 (EBeta window t-12..t-1, where each b(s) was fit on fRet = return of s+1, so the most recent return information is month t's return). Value is stamped at time_avail_m = t (month the MAs are observed); it predicts return in t+1. Monthly collapse of daily data: last trading row of the stock-month (sort permno,time_avail_m,time_d then .last()). save_predictor (save_standardized.py L32-83): drops rows where TrendFactor is NULL (polars is_not_null — NaN and inf are KEPT and written to CSV), yyyymm = year(time_avail_m)*100 + month(time_avail_m), columns [permno, yyyymm, TrendFactor].
specs.edge_semantics: (1) Null handling in filters: stata_ineq_pl treats null as +inf, so null prc and null mve_c pass their >= filters — replicate exactly. (2) Regression sample excludes inf AND NaN (np.isfinite), but the SIGNAL stage does NOT: A_L = inf (cfacpr==0) times finite EBeta -> inf TrendFactor, non-null, survives save; inf*0 EBeta -> NaN, survives save. (3) Collinear/constant regressors get beta = 0.0 exactly (not null); which member of a collinear set is dropped is QR-pivot dependent (largest-norm column kept), not first-column-wins. (4) Failed month regression -> NaN betas for that month; rolling_mean(min_samples=1) skips them; a 12-month stretch of all-failed months -> null EBeta -> that month's TrendFactor rows dropped by the ==11 gate. (5) fRet is a LEFT join from the filtered table itself: survivorship of the join target (t+1 filters) determines regression sample at t. (6) A_L rolling mean ignores nulls inside the window (mean of non-null) rather than propagating; monthly A_L is null iff last-day P null (division by null) or whole window null -> row dropped by ==11 gate. (7) betas_by_month rolling is positional over months present; missing calendar months compress the window. (8) stata_quantile with n==0 (no NYSE stocks in month) -> NaN qu10 -> only null-mve rows pass. (9) save_predictor drops only nulls, not NaN/inf.

specs.data_prep: Inputs: CCMLinkingTable.parquet [gvkey, permno, timeLinkStart_d, timeLinkEnd_d] (L30-31); m_QCompustat.parquet [gvkey, rdq] with rdq NaT dropped and (gvkey,rdq) dedup'd (L35-39); dailyCRSP.parquet [permno, time_d, ret] (L42-43); dailyFF.parquet [time_d, mktrf, rf] (L68-69). Pipeline: (a) LEFT merge daily CRSP with crosswalk on permno (L48) — a permno with multiple link rows MULTIPLIES daily rows; (b) keep rows with timeLinkStart_d <= time_d <= timeLinkEnd_d OR timeLinkEnd_d NaT (L52-56); rows with no link at all evaluate False and drop, so only linked permno-days survive; (c) gvkey pd.to_numeric coerce (L60); (d) LEFT merge announcement dates on (gvkey, time_d==rdq) with indicator; anndat = 1 iff rdq equals that EXACT calendar trading date (L61-62) — rdq on a weekend/holiday/non-trading day for that permno NEVER matches and the announcement is silently skipped; anndat is set BEFORE the FF merge; (e) INNER merge dailyFF on time_d (L70) — CRSP days without FF coverage drop (FF daily starts 1926-07; this also drops flagged announcement rows if FF lacks that date, erasing the whole event). Excess return: AnnouncementReturn_daily = ret - (mktrf + rf) (L73); NaN ret -> NaN. Business-day index: sort [permno, time_d], time_temp = groupby(permno).cumcount()+1 (L76-77) — positional over SURVIVING rows (post-link-filter, post-FF-inner-join), so 'days before/after' skip any dropped calendar days.
specs.window_mechanics: Event window is POSITIONAL, not calendar: rows with time_temp in [t0-2, t0+1] where t0 = time_temp of the announcement row (4 trading rows: 2 before, announcement day, 1 after — despite the header comment saying '3-day window'). Assignment (L89-111) via sequential np.where overwrites on time_ann_d: (1) anndat row -> t0; (2) row whose NEXT row is announcement (f1, shift(-1).fillna(0)) -> t0 (own+1); (3) row 2 before (f2, shift(-2)) -> t0 (own+2); (4) row 1 AFTER announcement (l1, shift(1)) -> t0 (own-1). Overlap precedence = LAST write wins: l1 > f2 > f1 > anndat. E.g. two announcements 3 rows apart: the middle row is both day-after of A and 2-days-before of B; l1 fires last so it belongs to A's window. Announcements 1 row apart: the first announcement's own row gets overwritten by f1 and joins the SECOND announcement's window. Rows outside every window (time_ann_d NaN) dropped (L114). No min-obs: at a stock's first row, the t0-2/t0-1 rows simply don't exist and the window is whatever rows survive; at the last row, t0+1 is missing and the window ends at t0. Verdict: fully positional over valid (surviving) rows; shifts use fillna(0) so group edges are safe.
specs.computation: Per (permno, t0) group (L121-125): AnnouncementReturn = SUM of daily excess returns over the window rows (pandas .agg 'sum': NaN days skipped, all-NaN group -> 0.0, min_count=0), and window_end_date = MAX time_d in the window. No regression, no dof. Simple arithmetic sum of ret - (mktrf + rf) over up to 4 trading rows.
specs.output_stamping: time_avail_m = calendar month (Period M) of MAX time_d in the window, i.e. normally the day AFTER the announcement (L123, L128) — an announcement on the last trading day of a month stamps the NEXT month (window spills), and one ending on the stock's final row stamps t0's month. Multiple windows collapsing to one permno-month: keep the LAST after stable sort by [permno, time_avail_m] (tail(1), L134-139) = the latest t0 in the month (lexsort is stable; prior order is ascending time_ann_d from the groupby). FORWARD FILL (L141-168): per permno, reindex to the FULL monthly range [min stamped month, max stamped month]; then for i=1..6 fill still-missing months from temp.shift(i) where temp is the ORIGINAL pre-fill series — so value(m) = original(m) if present, else original(m-j) for the smallest j in 1..6 with a non-null original; fills never compound and never extend past the stock's last announcement month. Then dropna (L169), yyyymm = year*100 + month (L176), save CSV [permno, yyyymm, AnnouncementReturn] sorted [permno, yyyymm] directly via to_csv (L184), NOT save_predictor — the dropna at L169 plays save_predictor's null-drop role.
specs.edge_semantics: (1) All-NaN-ret window -> pandas sum gives 0.0, which is saved as a real zero signal (not dropped). Partially-NaN windows sum only the non-NaN days. (2) Overlapping links: if the crosswalk has two gvkeys valid for the same permno-day, the daily row DUPLICATES after the L48 merge and survives twice; window sums then double-count — reference implicitly assumes non-overlapping link windows per permno. (3) rdq must equal an exact surviving trading date; otherwise the announcement produces nothing (no nearest-day snap). (4) The FF inner join can delete a flagged announcement row entirely, erasing its window (anndat computed pre-merge, window logic post-merge). (5) Overlap precedence between adjacent windows is the np.where order (l1 last): rows shared by two event windows go to the EARLIER announcement via l1, except the announcement row itself 1 day before another announcement goes to the LATER one via f1/f2. (6) inf: mktrf/rf/ret are never manipulated to produce inf; any inf would propagate through the sum and be saved (no isfinite filter anywhere). (7) Dedup: tempAnnDats dedup'd on (gvkey, rdq) so the L61 merge is 1:1 and row count is preserved. (8) time_avail_m NaT dropna at L132 is a no-op guard (time_d max always valid). (9) Fill mask is recomputed each i, so a month filled at i=1 is not overwritten at larger i.
